reading.body:
Equinix SV17 in Santa Clara is a confirmed active data center facility, but Equinix does not publish its power capacity or investment figures, limiting what can be measured about the building's role in AI infrastructure scaling.

The facility operates as part of Equinix's Silicon Valley metro campus, which claims over 10,500 customers including thousands of enterprises and network service providers. Six independent aggregator sources confirm its address and ongoing operation, even though Equinix's own index pages do not consistently list it. This suggests the company maintains substantial regional capacity without transparent disclosure of per-building metrics.

For tracking compute infrastructure and power constraints, this opacity matters. A data center's existence can be confirmed. Its power draw, cooling capacity, recent expansion, or utilization cannot. Equinix's specification sheets exist but require direct contact to obtain, placing detailed facility analysis outside public research workflows.

The Silicon Valley region hosts multiple Equinix facilities spanning Santa Clara, San Jose, Palo Alto, and Sunnyvale. Without published power figures for individual buildings, total regional capacity remains unmeasured, even for one of the world's largest colocation operators serving the geographic heart of AI development and deployment.
